creator: colton.deannn
title: Five built-in Claude Code commands: /rewind (undo to before Claude touched files), /compact (run at ~50% context), /context (see what fills the window), /output-style explanatory, /memory (edit CLAUDE.md rules)

tools.name: Claude Code /rewind
tools.detail: built-in command; jump back to before Claude touched anything

tools.name: Claude Code /compact
tools.detail: built-in; summarizes context; creator says run at ~50% context

tools.name: Claude Code /context
tools.detail: built-in; shows what is in the context window and how much remains

tools.name: Claude Code /output-style
tools.detail: built-in; 'explanatory' style makes Claude explain each decision while coding

tools.name: Claude Code /memory
tools.detail: built-in; opens the project memory file (CLAUDE.md) to set persistent rules

claims: /rewind returns the project to the state before Claude touched anything
/compact should be run around halfway through the context window to avoid 'context rot'
/context shows exactly what is in the context window and how much is left
/output-style explanatory makes Claude explain why it makes each decision; good when building something new
/memory sets rules once so Claude follows them every session, so you stop repeating yourself
how_to_steps: When Claude breaks something: /rewind to restore the pre-change state
Around 50% context usage: /compact to summarize the conversation
Check usage with /context before deciding whether to compact
On a new build: /output-style and choose Explanatory so it narrates its reasoning
Open /memory and write project rules into CLAUDE.md (e.g. TypeScript strict mode, run tests before commit, match existing code style)

relevance.why: All five are real built-in Claude Code commands and the '/compact at ~50%' and 'explanatory output style for new builds' habits are useful, but a veteran Claude Code user likely already knows /compact, /context and /memory.

implement_score.why: Zero install cost. Worth adopting: check /context and compact proactively near 50%, use /output-style explanatory on unfamiliar builds, and keep rules in CLAUDE.md via /memory. The rewind guidance is handy but the UI shown is a mock-up.
